The contrast media is given through a small needle placed into a vein, usually on the elbow or on the back of your hand. Normally,
contrast media is considered quite safe, however, any injection carries slight risk of harm including injury to a nerve, artery or vela,
infection, or reaction to the material being injected Occasionally, a patient will have # mild reaction to the contrast agent like
nausea, vomiting, rash or itching. Uncommonly ( one case in . thousand) a serious reaction to the contrast occurs like difficulty in
breathing, respiratory arrest, cardiac arrest, fits or kidney dysfunction. Rarely, intravenous contrast can leak our from vein into soft
tissue (incidence is 0.2-0.4%) and can cause skin discolouration, pain, numbnoss or death of tissue and very rarely requires surgery
for the same. The physicians and staff of the hospital are trained to treat these reactions. Very rarely (1.75000) death has occurred
related to contrast administration; the risk of such . severe consequence is similar to that from the administration of penicillin
Certain patients are an higher risk for experiencing a reaction to the contrast agent.
